observed_anchor: The Zhengguo canal and dam turned a saline area east of Xianyang into a more reliable irrigated farming zone.
interpretation: The conquest state first enlarged the productive base around its core rather than merely requisitioning grain after harvest.
limits: The row does not estimate irrigated hectares annual yields workers or Qin's causal share in victory.

observed_anchor: Qin expanded the Dujiangyan irrigation system after conquering Sichuan and linked an agricultural colony to further imperial expansion.
input: river water conquered land and relocated households
output: redirect regional surplus toward a wider state
interpretation: Infrastructure could transform both landscapes and political relationships in newly conquered territory.
limits: Chronology and mechanism are stronger than any surviving annual output or transported-grain total; colonial transformation was not locally costless.

observed_anchor: The Ling Canal crossed the Nanling watershed and connected the Xiang and Li river systems during Qin's campaign into Lingnan.
input: existing river corridors plus cut canal
interpretation: A short artificial link could make much longer natural corridors usable as one transport system.
limits: The source establishes connectivity and strategic context not cargo volume travel time construction workforce or uninterrupted use.

observed_anchor: The Record of Travel Routes preserves 41 entries: 34 inter-place distances and seven section lengths along a south–north corridor used for long-distance grain shipment.
input: grain boats roads waterways and measured legs
interpretation: Logistics became repeatable when routes were recorded as linked legs rather than remembered as one journey.
limits: The itinerary is unusually detailed but does not preserve shipment tonnage cadence loss rates exact modern geometry or a universal Qin road map.

observed_anchor: A Dongting order required Qianling's commander granary and communes to report whether rations were sufficient for soldiers guarding troops and hard laborers by a fixed deadline.
input: granary stocks people registers and messenger chain
output: identify shortages before the year ended
interpretation: A granary was an information office as well as a building: food became administratively useful when obligations and stocks could be compared.
limits: One surviving directive shows a reporting procedure and shortage risk not county-wide consumption delivery success or total personnel.

evidence_class: excavated storage archaeology and documentary synthesis
observed_anchor: The main storage of the Western Han Capital Granary likely exceeded 10000 cubic metres and had at least five subsidiary storage sites.
input: tax grain transport and storage buildings
output: support a capital and wider redistribution network
interpretation: Storage scale increased under Han as waterways into Chang'an improved; imperial logistics was an evolving system rather than a finished Qin blueprint.
limits: The Qin Grand Granary has not been found. The Han capacity is approximate and is not converted here into soldier-months people fed or annual throughput.

observed_anchor: Early Han water-control law and repair documents show officials working with local communities to maintain dikes canals and other hydraulic infrastructure.
input: official rules local knowledge and recurring labor
output: keep fields settlements and corridors usable
interpretation: Imperial infrastructure depended on recurrent local coordination after construction; central authority did not replace community knowledge or labor.
limits: Much evidence is early Han. Qin legal ancestry is plausible but cannot make every later rule a direct Qin survival or quantify annual labor.

input: registered and penal labor plus grain tools and supervision

interpretation: The same machinery that extended reach could overload households and erode consent; logistics created vulnerability as well as capacity.
limits: The transmitted 700000-worker palace-and-mausoleum figure is not accepted as a measured workforce and no wall length annual labor share mortality or revolt-causation score is reconstructed.
